newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ bank bills close offered as currency comes off.
newsitem.headline: NZ bank bills close offered as currency comes off.

text.p: New Zealand bank bills ended offered on Wednesday after the currency was sold in late trading.
Dealers said the bills had been well bid as the Trade-Weighted Index approached 68.50 but when an offshore player sold a largish parcel of Kiwi the bills came back to Tuesday's closing levels.
Traders said the market was watching the TWI for direction these days.
"The tone is bearish," a dealer said. He said monetary conditions were still considered tight and risk was on the upside for yields.
Futures selling fed through into the physical market.
The bond market was lethargic and traders fear it will stay that way for some time.
One said the 11/06s were locked in a 7.20-40 range and external influences were the most important at present.
The main debate was whether the Reserve Bank would allow a further easing in the next quarter and the market was evenly balanced in its view on that.
